title: A Baby in a Basket
bigQuestion: How does the story say a baby in a basket grew up to be a leader?

story.title: The Basket in the Reeds
story.kicker: A mother makes a little boat, and a big sister watches from the tall grass.
paragraphs: The river was wide and slow. Tall reeds grew along the edge. A mother knelt by the water. She held a basket made of reeds. She had painted it with tar so no water could get in. Inside the basket was her baby boy.
The mother kissed the baby. She set the basket in the reeds. The water rocked it softly. Then she walked away. Her heart was full of worry. She did not know what would happen next.
A girl hid in the tall grass. She was the baby's big sister. She did not move. She did not make a sound. She watched the basket. She waited to see who would come.
This is a story from the book of Exodus. Exodus is the second book of the Bible. Jews and Christians tell this story. Muslims tell a story of this baby too. His name was Moses.
story.think: The big sister stayed to watch the basket. Why do you think she stayed?

lessons.title: Many, Many People
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Jacob's family grew into a big people in Egypt.
reading: Remember Joseph? His family moved to *Egypt*. Egypt is a land by a long river. The river is called the Nile. The family had food there.
Years went by. The family grew and grew. The story says they became a big people. They were called the Israelites. That name comes from Jacob. Jacob was also called Israel.
Exodus is the book that tells this. It is the second book of the Bible. The first chapter says the Israelites filled the land.

words.d: a land in Africa by the Nile River, where the story says Jacob's family went to live
the big family of Jacob, who was also called Israel; the people in the Exodus story

look.title: Picture a Family Growing
look.text: Picture one big tent. Inside are Jacob's twelve sons and their children. Now picture many years going by. There are hundreds of tents. Then thousands. Children run between them. A whole town of one family fills the land by the river.
look.prompt: How did one family turn into a whole people? Tell it in your own words.

check.q: Where did Jacob's family live in the Exodus story?
check.why: The story says Jacob's family moved to Egypt in Joseph's time and grew there.

check.q: What book of the Bible tells the story of Moses?
check.why: Exodus is the second book of the Bible. It tells the story of Moses.

check.q: What does the name Israelites come from?
choices: Jacob, who was also called Israel
check.why: Jacob was given the name Israel. His family became the Israelites.

lessons.title: A New King Says Work
lessons.mainIdea: The story says a new king made the Israelites work as slaves.
reading: A new king came to rule Egypt. The king of Egypt was called *Pharaoh*. Pharaoh did not know Joseph. He looked at the Israelites. He saw how many they were. He was afraid.
So Pharaoh made them *slaves*. A slave is a person who is not free. The Israelites had to make bricks. They had to build cities. They worked all day in the hot sun.
The story says Pharaoh made a cruel rule too. It put the Israelite baby boys in danger. Two brave helpers said no to the king. Their names were Shiphrah and Puah.

words.d: the name for the king of Egypt
people who are not free and are made to work for someone else

look.title: The Story Says
look.text: A new king came to rule Egypt. He did not know Joseph. He said the Israelites were too many. So he made them work very hard. They built cities for him. But the more they were pushed down, the more they grew.
look.cite: Exodus 1, retold in simple words from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: Why was the new king afraid of the Israelites?

check.q: What is a Pharaoh?
check.why: In the story, Pharaoh is the name for the king of Egypt.

check.q: What did the Israelites have to do as slaves?
check.why: Exodus 1 says they made bricks and built cities for Pharaoh.

check.q: Who said no to the king's cruel rule?
check.why: Exodus 1 names two helpers, Shiphrah and Puah, who did not obey the king.

lessons.title: A Mother's Plan
lessons.mainIdea: The story says a mother hid her baby in a basket on the river to keep him safe.
reading: A mother had a baby boy. She saw he was a fine baby. She hid him for three months. But a baby cries. She could not hide him forever.
So she made a plan. She made a *basket* out of reeds. She painted it with tar. Now water could not get in. She put the baby inside. She set it in the reeds by the *Nile*.
The baby's sister stood far off. She watched to see what would happen. The story says her name was Miriam.

words.d: a container woven from reeds or straw; in the story it floats like a little boat
the long river that runs through Egypt

look.title: A Basket That Floats
look.text: Look at a basket made of reeds. It has holes between the reeds. Water would leak in. Now look at the same basket painted with black, sticky tar. The holes are filled. Now it floats like a little boat.
look.prompt: Why did the mother paint the basket with tar? What would happen without it?

check.q: How long did the mother hide her baby at home?
check.why: Exodus 2 says she hid him for three months before she made the basket.

check.q: What was the basket made of?
check.why: The story says the basket was made of reeds and covered with tar.

check.q: Who watched the basket from far off?
check.why: Exodus 2 says the baby's sister stood far off to watch.

lessons.title: A Princess Finds a Baby
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Pharaoh's daughter found the baby and named him Moses.
reading: Pharaoh's daughter came to the river. She wanted to wash. She saw the basket in the reeds. She opened it. The baby was crying. She felt sorry for him.
Then the sister ran up. She said, "Shall I find a woman to feed the baby?" The princess said yes. The sister ran and got her own mother! So the baby's mother took care of him.
When he was bigger, he went to live with the princess. She named him *Moses*. The story says the name means "I pulled him out of the water."

words.d: the baby found in the basket; the story says his name means pulled out of the water

look.title: Out of the Water
look.text: Pharaoh's daughter saw the basket in the reeds. She sent a helper to get it. She opened it and saw the baby. He was crying. She felt sorry for him. She said, "This is one of the Hebrew children." Later she named him Moses, because she pulled him out of the water.
look.cite: Exodus 2:5-10, retold in simple words from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: The princess knew the baby was an Israelite. She kept him anyway. What does that tell you about her?

check.q: Who found the baby in the basket?
check.why: Exodus 2 says Pharaoh's daughter came to the river and found the basket.

check.q: Who took care of the baby while he was little?
check.why: The sister brought the baby's own mother, and the princess let her care for him.

check.q: What does the story say the name Moses means?
check.why: Exodus 2:10 says the princess named him Moses because she pulled him out of the water.

lessons.title: Moses Runs Away
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Moses grew up, got in trouble, and ran away to a far land.
reading: Moses grew up in Pharaoh's house. But he knew he was an Israelite. One day he saw a man hitting an Israelite slave. Moses got very angry. He hit the man hard, and the man died.
Pharaoh heard about it. He wanted to punish Moses. So Moses ran away. He went to a far land called *Midian*.
In Midian, Moses sat by a well. He helped some sisters get water for their sheep. Their father was glad. Moses married one sister. Her name was Zipporah. Moses became a *shepherd*.

words.d: the far land where the story says Moses lived after he ran away from Egypt
a person who takes care of sheep

look.title: From a Palace to a Field
look.text: Picture Moses in Pharaoh's house. He has nice clothes and lots of food. Now picture Moses in Midian. He walks in the dust all day with sheep. He sleeps in a tent. His life is very different now.
look.prompt: How was Moses's life in Midian different from his life in Egypt?

check.q: Why did Moses run away from Egypt?
choices: He wanted to see the sea
He got in trouble with Pharaoh
check.why: Exodus 2 says Moses hurt a man, and Pharaoh wanted to punish him, so he ran.

check.q: Where did Moses go when he ran away?
check.why: The story says Moses went to the land of Midian.

check.q: What job did Moses do in Midian?
check.why: Exodus 3 says Moses kept the sheep of his wife's father.

lessons.title: The Bush That Kept Burning
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Moses saw a bush on fire that did not burn up, and heard God speak.
reading: One day Moses led the sheep to a mountain. He saw a bush on fire. But the bush did not burn up! Moses went closer to look.
The story says God spoke to Moses from the bush. God said, "Take off your shoes. This is *holy* ground." Holy means set apart and special.
Then the story says God told Moses a job. "My people are hurting in Egypt. Go to Pharaoh. Bring my people out." Moses was scared. He said, "Who am I to do this?"

words.d: set apart as special; in the story, the ground near the bush was holy

look.title: Holy Ground
look.text: Moses saw a bush burning with fire. But the bush was not burned up. He said, "I will go and see this strange thing." Then the story says God called to him from the bush: "Moses, Moses!" And Moses said, "Here I am."
look.cite: Exodus 3:2-4, retold in simple words from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: What did Moses see that was strange? What did he say when God called his name?

check.q: What was strange about the bush?
choices: It was on fire but did not burn up
check.why: Exodus 3 says the bush burned with fire but was not burned up.

check.q: What does holy mean?
check.why: Holy means set apart as special. God told Moses the ground was holy.

check.q: What job did the story say God gave Moses?
choices: Go to Pharaoh and bring the people out
check.why: In Exodus 3, God sends Moses to Pharaoh to bring the Israelites out of Egypt.

lessons.title: Let My People Go
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Moses went back to Egypt to tell Pharaoh to let the people go.
reading: Moses did not feel brave. He said, "I am not good at talking." The story says God gave him a helper. It was his brother, *Aaron*. Aaron could speak well.
So Moses went back to Egypt. He was old now. Aaron went with him. They stood in front of Pharaoh. They gave him a *message*. A message is words you carry for someone else.
The message was short. "Let my people go." Jews, Christians and Muslims all tell this part. The Qur'an calls Moses by the name Musa.

words.d: Moses's brother, who spoke for him in the story
words you carry to someone from someone else

look.title: The Message to Pharaoh
look.text: Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness.
look.prompt: Who is the message from, and who carried it? Say it in your own words.

check.q: Who helped Moses talk to Pharaoh?
check.why: Exodus 4 says Aaron would speak for Moses because Moses said he was not good at talking.

check.q: What was the message to Pharaoh?
check.why: In Exodus 5, Moses and Aaron tell Pharaoh, "Let my people go."

check.q: What name does the Qur'an use for Moses?
check.why: The Qur'an tells the story of Moses too, and calls him Musa.

review.q: Which book of the Bible tells the story of Moses?
review.why: Exodus, the second book of the Bible, tells the story of Moses.

review.q: Why did Pharaoh make the Israelites slaves?
choices: He saw how many they were and was afraid
review.why: Exodus 1 says the new king was afraid because the Israelites were so many.

review.q: Where did the mother put the basket?
choices: In the reeds by the Nile
review.why: Exodus 2 says she set the basket in the reeds by the river.

review.q: Who watched from far off to see what would happen?
review.why: The baby's sister, later called Miriam, watched from far off.

review.q: Where did the story say God spoke to Moses?
review.why: Exodus 3 says God spoke to Moses from a bush that burned but did not burn up.

review.q: What did Moses and Aaron tell Pharaoh?
review.why: In Exodus 5, they carry the message, "Let my people go."
